newsitem.title: GERMANY: Porsche races to higher profits.
newsitem.headline: Porsche races to higher profits.

text.p: German sports-car maker Porsche said Thursday that it accelerated to unexpectedly higher profits in its 1995-96 business year and would consider resuming a dividend payout for the first time since 1992.
The legendary Stuttgart-based carmaker said it expected to report a profit of about 40 million to 50 million marks ($26 million to $33 million) for its 1995-96 business year that ended July 31.

Porsche's profit during the first six months of the year totalled 10.3 million marks ($6.7 million). The higher profits in the second half were due to cost-saving measures along with strong demand for the popular 911 model, the carmaker said.
Porsche hinted at signs of the strong recovery in January when it said sales were gaining and later said in August that profits would be at least 25 million marks ($16 million).
But Porsche's profit, particularly when compared to the 1994-95 level of 2.1 million marks ($1.4 million) was still above market expectations, analysts said.
Sales rose to about 2.8 billion marks ($1.8 billion) compared with 2.61 billion marks ($1.7 billion) in 1994-95. Porsche said final results for the year will be released on Nov. 6.

Porsche also said its supervisory board would also decide at a meeting on Nov. 6 on whether to resume paying a dividend for the first time since it paid out 2.50 marks ($1.60) for each of its preference shares for the 1991-92 business year.
